chapter: Three Deuces and 52nd Street with Tatum
title: Hometown, parents, and his birth date
summary: He went back to Virginia once, knew his parents little, sold papers as a boy, and worked at a cleaning and pressing shop.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did you ever get a chance to travel back to your old home town?
Virginia you mean. No, I went back there once, that was enough for me.
You don't have any family there at all?
To digress a bit... Did you know your parents at all?

No I didn't know them that well. She stayed in the Church a lot, and I was out in the street. Shiniw shoes -- I'd be gettin' up 5 o'clock in the mornin' sellin' newspapers -- The Times-Herald. I did the regular hustle that the fellows do. There was no robbin' and stealin' like they do now...
Date of birth sometimes given at 1917, not 1916 as you said before.

Well, to me that's approximately right, although I remember when I was real young and still footin' around with the piano I had a little job at a cleaning & pressing place called Joe Frank's. It was like over town you would call it, -- other side of the bridge and tracks -- when you went over the bridge and tracks you were in the white neighborhood. So somehow or other I got a job working for -- they gave me a little Ford that I wrecked about ten times. A little truck, to deliver clothes. I could keep whatever cleaning that I got, and that was the deal. I didn't get no salary. I learned how to press clothes. I pressed clothes in Washington -- If I had stayed down there I'd have did a lot better much better than I'm doing up here, I'll tell you. 'Cause I would have had a cleaning and pressing joint -- establishment, Because I knew the business, I'd see how they dyed, and all the equipment --
